A.why: Reward for cost-saving suggestions is a classic Initiative illustration; the stem names it as part of the setup.

B.why: Using 'we' not 'I' reflects Esprit de corps, but it is only one of the two described practices.

C.why: Nothing about one plan/one head for a group of activities.

D.why: No mention of concentration of decision authority.

items.missing_decisive_condition: Stem gives two practices (suggestion reward system, 'we' usage) pointing to different principles; it does not say which one is tested.
items.quality_note: Two-clue stem makes both Initiative and Esprit de corps defensible; ambiguous.
items.source_explanation: No excerpts supplied. 'We' instead of 'I' points to Esprit de corps (B), but a suggestion system rewarding cost cutting equally points to Initiative (A). Unity of direction and Centralisation are not shown. As two options are defensible, there is no single answer.

A.why: Debt is cheaper than equity, so cost falls.

B.why: Cheaper debt lowers overall cost with equity cost unchanged; fixed interest charges and financial risk rise.

C.why: Interest and principal repayment are obligatory, so risk rises.

D.why: Equity is not riskless; risk rises with debt.

items.source_explanation: No excerpts supplied. Debt is cheaper than equity, so with equity cost unchanged overall cost falls, while fixed interest obligations raise financial risk (B). A reverses the cost relation, C wrongly says repayment is not obligatory, D wrongly calls equity riskless.

A.why: Consumer Protection Act 2019: appeal from District Commission to State Commission within 45 days.

items.quality_note: Factual recall; clear. Relies on the 2019 Act, which the stem does not name.
items.source_explanation: No excerpts supplied. Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 an appeal against a District Commission order lies to the State Commission within 45 days (A); 30, 60 and 15 days are not the statutory period.

A.why: Education is broad theoretical learning, not a job-skill programme.

B.why: Development is broader long-term growth, mostly managerial; a skills and knowledge programme could loosely fit.

D.why: Training is a short programme improving knowledge and skills for a job.

items.missing_decisive_condition: Whether the programme is job-specific (training) or overall growth (development) is not stated.
items.quality_note: Training is the best fit but Development is a plausible rival; weak discrimination.
items.source_explanation: No excerpts supplied. A three-week programme building skills and knowledge best matches Training (D). Education and Selection do not fit. Development is not clearly excluded since the stem gives no job-specific or long-term cue.

A.why: Planning in June then continuous monitoring and timely briefing shows an ongoing process.

B.why: Coordination being all pervasive is true in general but the scenario does not illustrate it.

C.why: Contradicted by continuous monitoring after planning.

D.why: Contradicted: coordination is needed at all levels.

items.quality_note: Clear scenario; B is a general truth so not strictly refuted, but A is the best illustration.
items.source_explanation: No excerpts supplied. Continuous monitoring after an initial plan illustrates coordination as a continuous process (A). C is contradicted by that monitoring and D is false as coordination applies at all levels. B is true generally but is not what the scenario shows.

A.why: Management by exception means only significant deviations are examined, saving time.

B.why: It encourages delegation, not hinders it.

C.why: Management by exception saves managerial time and focuses attention on key areas.

D.why: Not a recognised consequence; it aids delegation and motivation.

items.source_explanation: No excerpts supplied. Looking only at deviations beyond the permissible limit is management by exception, which saves time and focuses on important areas (C). A contradicts it, B and D reverse its effect on delegation and morale.

A.why: (i) and (iii) are inputs received from the environment.

D.why: Taxes paid and returns paid to investors are outputs supplied to the environment.

items.quality_note: Clear; relies on the textbook classification the stem invokes.
items.source_explanation: No excerpts supplied. Finance and power/water are inputs drawn from the environment; tax payments and return on investment are outputs supplied to it, so (ii) and (iv) (D). A, B and C each include an input.

B.why: Barnard says it may contribute to joint results; not 'only when'.

C.why: Conscious purpose characterises formal, not informal, organisation.

D.why: Davis: network of relationships not established or required by formal organisation, arising spontaneously.

items.quality_note: Good; B is a subtle distractor distorting Barnard.
items.source_explanation: No excerpts supplied. Barnard calls it joint personal activity without conscious joint purpose, and Davis a network of relationships not established or required by the formal organisation (D). A and C describe formal organisation; B distorts 'may contribute' into 'only when'.

A.why: 10,000 + 4x1,800 = 17,200; fixed salary (time based) plus per-unit incentive.

B.why: 7,200 omits salary and the plan is not performance only.

C.why: 10,000 omits incentive; plan is not time based only.

D.why: Total is right but a direct incentive is not an indirect payment like insurance.

items.source_explanation: No excerpts supplied. Total pay is 10,000 + 7,200 = Rs 17,200, combining a fixed time-based salary with a per-unit incentive (A). B and C drop a component; D has the right amount but wrongly classifies direct pay as indirect.
